newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo farm debt should not become public debt - paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo farm debt should not become public debt - paper.

text.p: Transforming Yugoslavia's farm debt into public debt could be disastrous for the country's financial system, Belgrade daily Nasa Borba said on Tuesday.

"Transforming farm debt into public debt would only confirm a wrong financial-monetary policy. Why go for a public debt and repay something that need not be repaid at all," the paper quoted Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic as saying.

Djunic said the government was now preparing a programme to release frozen hard currency savings, but would not recognize unrealistically high interest paid by crashed pyramid savings schemes such as Dafiment bank and some other banks.
"The borrowed capital must carry more realistic interest rates and that would be the farmers' debt which they will repay to banks," Djunic said.
"If we had accepted the farm debt as public debt, we would be accepting to pay banks the 'wild' interest. That would be a disaster as far as the system is concerned," Djunic said.

Total debt of primary agricultural production to banks has reached almost two billion dinars ($358 million), after initial debt of 650 million dinars in 1995 grew three-fold becuase of transforming due principle and high interest into new credits.

According to a proposed law, the amount of debt as of December 31, 1996 is taken as the principle debt. The draft envisages 10-year repayment period starting from the year 2000, preceeded by a three-year grace period.
Over the period, the state would have to repay around five billion dinars in principle and accumulated interest. Funds would be secured from income taxes and excise duties.

The draft was proposed by Jugoagrar association of agricultural producers and supported by the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia and Yugoslav parliament agriculture committee. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
